# "ADDR name" pairs for the interactive disassembler:
#
#     id> loadbin snapshot.bin 0
#     id> labels ../decoded/neptune/testdata/labels.txt
#     id> dis $3523 $3540
#
# It is also the working list for step 6.1 of docs/decompiling/playbook.md,
# which is where these names reach the C.
#
# THE RULE FOR THIS FILE
#
# "A name asserting something unproven is worse than no name." Every line below
# carries its evidence, and an address whose purpose is merely suspected is
# deliberately absent -- 84 functions have address-derived names in neptune.c
# and only the ones here have earned better.

# --- the top level ---------------------------------------------------------
# Four main loops, each ending by jumping through its own zero-page vector.
# Derived in step 2 from the routine report's rejections plus the vector values
# in the captured image; see README.md.
2000 main_loop_via_36        # JMP ($36); $36/$37 holds $2000
2080 main_loop_via_38        # JMP ($38); $38/$39 holds $2080
2100 main_loop_via_4e        # JMP ($4E); $4E/$4F holds $2100
2180 main_loop_via_3a        # JMP ($3A); $3A/$3B holds $2180

# --- state transitions -----------------------------------------------------
# The four loops above are game states, and a routine can end the current state
# by jumping into the head of another. $1A4C, inside $0E00's block set, is one:
#
#   1A4C: JMP $2079
#   2079: LDA #$01 / STA $A0 / JSR $3800  -> falls into main_loop_via_38
#
# $A0 is the state variable the loops set. Named for the mechanism rather than
# the meaning: which state is which is not established yet.
2079 enter_state_via_38
00A0 state_var

# --- the title screen ------------------------------------------------------
# $3523 is where neptune.b33 starts. STA KBDSTRB, then 256 rounds of
# poll-and-delay; a key branches to $3580 and a timeout falls through to the
# attract demo at $3535. Read directly off the disassembly.
3523 title_wait_for_input
3528 title_wait_loop
3570 delay_one_tick           # LDA #$40, JSR MON_WAIT, JSR $AEC0
3580 title_input_seen         # BMI target: something was pressed
3535 title_timed_out          # falls through to the attract demo

# --- input mode selection --------------------------------------------------
# $3584 reads the two joystick buttons and the keyboard, and then *writes code*
# into three sites, which is what the collector's 21 generations are. The bytes
# it pokes decode as the instructions named below, so the naming is derivation
# rather than inference.
3584 poll_input_select_mode
3700 patch_input_joystick     # writes AD 61 C0 / AD 62 C0 = LDA $C061 / $C062
359A patch_input_keyboard     # writes AD 00 C0 = LDA $C000, CMP #$C1, CMP #$DA

# The three sites those patches rewrite. Named for what they are rather than
# what they do, because what they do is whichever patch last ran.
1060 input_site_a
1300 input_site_b
138C input_site_c

# --- hi-res drawing --------------------------------------------------------
# Verified in testdata/known-data.txt: all 192 entries reproduce the standard
# hi-res row address formula for base $4000, and none of them for $2000.
0C00 tbl_hgr_row_hi
0D00 tbl_hgr_row_lo
3876 erase_sprite_row         # reads the row tables, EOR #$FF / AND / STA

# --- the player's gun ------------------------------------------------------
# $1380 is the fire control, and $138C inside it is one of the three sites
# poll_input_select_mode patches. Read straight off the disassembly: it compares
# the key against #$C1, which is 'A' with bit 7 set, and 'A' is the fire key on
# the disk's own help screen.
#
# On a press it seeds a shot -- sets the active flag, builds a screen pointer
# from tbl_hgr_row_hi/lo indexed by $E0+6, and zeroes the spacing counter $CC.
# There are three shot slots, and $CC spaces them: $13B8 increments it and arms
# the second at 8 and the third at $10.
#
#   slot 1  $C0 active, $C1/$C2 screen pointer, $C3 column, $BD row index
#   slot 2  $C4 active, $C5/$C6 pointer,        $C7 column, $BE
#   slot 3  $C8 active, $C9/$CA pointer,        $CB column, $BF
#
# $1400 then draws and erases them: EOR #$FF / AND ($C1),Y against a mask at
# $1350,Y, stepping the column to #$28 -- 40 bytes, the width of the screen.
# That is the "magenta dashes travelling across the upper screen" in
# docs/neptune.md, and it is why the gun fires horizontally.
1380 fire_control
13B8 shot_advance_slots
1400 shots_draw
1350 tbl_shot_mask

# --- Joystick mode ---------------------------------------------------------
# Reached only when $3700 has patched `JSR $36B0` into $1060, which happens
# when exactly one button is held at the title screen. See code-at.txt for why
# $36B0 needs a --code-at root to be decoded at all.
36B0 paddle_read_axis
3040 paddle_invert_vertical

# The two axis deltas the input routines produce, and the position they move.
# Which axis is which is not taken from the paddle-numbering convention; it is
# read off the consumers. $E3 drives $E0 alone, clamped to [$08..$9D] -- a
# scanline range. $E4 drives $E1/$E2, where $E2 wraps at 7 and carries into
# $E1, which is the 7-pixels-per-byte HGR column layout. So $E3 is vertical and
# $E4 is horizontal, and $3040 -- which swaps the immediates at $36CD and $36DB,
# both in the arm that stores $E3 -- inverts the vertical axis.
#
# $E0 and $E4 otherwise disassemble as ERR_UNDEFFUNC and HGRCOLOR, which are
# Applesoft's zero-page names leaking in from the symbol database. Neptune is
# not Applesoft and does not mean either thing.
00E0 player_y
00E1 player_col
00E2 player_subx
00E3 axis_vertical
00E4 axis_horizontal

# --- ROM -------------------------------------------------------------------
# The only ROM entry point the game calls; see testdata/rom.externs.
FCA8 rom_mon_wait
